subject: Post-call recap & competitive bake-off next steps (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & competitive bake-off next steps (Acme Health)

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Key pain points you shared:
- High per-token inference costs on burst traffic for summarization workflows
- Inconsistent latency during end-of-day batch processing windows
- Desire to pin models and have predictable SLAs for regulated PHI workloads

Goals you mentioned:
- Consistent 99th percentile latency under 300ms for interactive flows
- Reduce inference cost by ~30% through batching/caching or quantization
- Full SOC 2 evidence and support for customer-managed keys for PHI

Competitive bake-off context:
- You’re evaluating Redwood, VendorX, and CloudAI; decision criteria focus on latency, cost, security (KMS + audit logs), and ease of deployment into Acme’s VPC.

Open questions we agreed to validate during the bake-off:
1) Can Redwood meet the 99th percentile latency SLO for your interactive summarization (avg seq len ~512 tokens)?
2) What token-cost delta should you expect vs. VendorX for peak traffic with continuous batching?
3) Can we demonstrate KMS integration and provide SOC 2 artifacts within your procurement timeline?

Proposed next steps (from Redwood):
- Share a preliminary bake-off matrix (attached) that outlines test cases, metrics, and pass criteria.
- Run a 3-day comparative test of the summarization workload (we’ll provide a test harness and can run in your dev VPC or our dedicated instance).
- Provide SOC 2 and KMS integration docs (attached: redwood-sla.pdf).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with Rishi and your infra lead to kick off the test (propose Thu 3/5 or Fri 3/6).

Please confirm the proposed next steps and which date works for the tech kickoff. Happy to adjust tests to match the scenarios you care about.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: acme-bakeoff-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-sla.pdf (pdf)
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@acmehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & competitive bake-off next steps (Acme Health)

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the thorough recap. That aligns with what we heard internally. A few clarifications: 

- Our interactive summarization traffic peaks at 800rps with many short-lived sessions; 512 tokens is a good estimate for average sequence length. For latency SLOs we care about p95/p99 — if you can show p99 < 300ms in a realistic test that will check a big box for us.
- Cost target: we’re not fixed on 30% but we need demonstrable unit-cost savings over VendorX’s managed endpoint pricing.
- For security: we need KMS + proof of data-in-transit encryption and an audit log sample. SOC 2 report should be available for vendor review — procurement will confirm exact artifacts needed.

Tech kickoff: Thu 3/5 10:00am PT works for Carlos and me.

For the bake-off matrix: please include the exact scripts/requests you’ll run so we can mirror in VendorX tests. We’ll also share a small redacted dataset for the test.

Thanks,

Alicia
Director of Product, Acme Health
alicia.gomez@acmehealth.com
